text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., under federal investigation for fraudulent Medicare billing, said late Friday that its chief financial officer has resigned.
In a one-sentence news release, the company said Robert Stearns, who was "hired by the previous management" on July 21, has resigned effective Aug. 31.
Company officials were not immediately available.

A four-month-old investigation by several federal agencies led last month to raids on 33 company facilities in six states and seizures of cartloads of files pertaining to laboratory billing and home health care.

Three Columbia managers were indicted on fraud charges last week. Shareholders have filed at least 11 lawsuits against the firm and the attorneys general of Florida, Texas and Alabama are investigating the firm.
Columbia's former chief executive and its president were ousted on July 24 by a board of directors angry about the handling of the probe.
It was not clear if the company had appointed an interim chief financial officer or was searching for a successor.
